claim: Lung cancer is the most common cancer among all human tumor types, with more than 1.7 × 10^6 new cases worldwide each year.
source: Lung cancer is the most common cancer among all human tumor types, with more than 1.7 × 106 new cases worldwide each year.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published data (Siegel et al., 2020) as indicated in the manuscript.

claim: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) accounts for most lung cancers according to the Global Cancer Report data.
source: According to the Global Cancer Report data, lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) accounts for most lung cancers (Siegel et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the Global Cancer Report (Siegel et al., 2020).

claim: The application of adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NCT) has significantly improved the long-term survival of LUAD patients.
source: The application of adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NCT) has significantly improved the long-term survival of LUAD patients.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation (Ren et al., 2021) as indicated in the manuscript.

claim: Chemotherapy drugs are highly toxic and can often become ineffective.
source: However, chemotherapy drugs are highly toxic and can often become ineffective (Ekoh et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Ekoh et al., 2022).

claim: Continued ineffective chemotherapy will lead to the generation of drug-resistant tumor cell clones.
source: In addition, continued ineffective chemotherapy will lead to the generation of drug-resistant tumor cell clones (Cai et al., 2020; Bondarenko et al., 2021) and a delay in tumor removal.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Cai et al., 2020; Bondarenko et al., 2021).

claim: Almost all cancer patients show inherent or acquired drug resistance, leading to treatment failure and unsatisfactory overall survival.
source: Almost all cancer patients show inherent or acquired drug resistance, leading to treatment failure and unsatisfactory overall survival.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge about cancer drug resistance.

claim: The TME has been proved to be an essential source of intratumoral heterogeneity.
source: Many studies have increasingly proved the TME to be an essential source of intratumoral heterogeneity (Katsumata et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Katsumata et al., 2018).

claim: Consuming glucose in TME by cancer cells may promote nutritional competition, a metabolic mechanism of immunosuppression.
source: Formerly, it was generally believed that consuming glucose in TME by cancer cells may promote nutritional competition, a metabolic mechanism of immunosuppression (Ho et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Ho et al., 2015).

claim: Tumor-infiltrating immune cells rely on glucose for their energy needs and functionality, with immune cells, particularly macrophages, consuming more glucose than malignant cells.
source: However, recent studies have shown that tumor-infiltrating immune cells rely on glucose for their energy needs and functionality, with immune cells, particularly macrophages, consuming more glucose than malignant cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent studies (Chang et al., 2015) as indicated in the manuscript.

claim: The impaired immune cell metabolism in the TME helps tumor cells escape immunity.
source: The impaired immune cell metabolism in the TME helps tumor cells escape immunity (Chang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Chang et al., 2015).

claim: The selective cellular allocation of nutrients can be used to develop therapeutic and imaging strategies to enhance or monitor the metabolic processes and activities of specific cell populations in TME.
source: It is believed that the selective cellular allocation of these nutrients can be used to develop therapeutic and imaging strategies to enhance or monitor the metabolic processes and activities of specific cell populations in TME (Reinfeld et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Reinfeld et al., 2021).

claim: A total of 83,622 cells were enrolled for subsequent analyses in this study.
source: A total of 83,622 cells were enrolled for subsequent analyses.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: After quality control, 33,567 cells were derived from the control group and 50,055 cells from the NCT group.
source: After quality control, a total of 83,622 cells that met the inclusion criteria were subjected to subsequent analyses, with 33,567 and 50,055 cells derived from the control and NCT groups, respectively (Figure 1a–c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and referenced in Figure 1.

claim: The composition of cell types exhibited high heterogeneity across different groups.
source: The composition of cell types exhibited high heterogeneity across different groups.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Functional enrichment analysis revealed that chemotherapy drove significant metabolic reprogramming in tumor cells and macrophages.
source: Functional enrichment analysis revealed that chemotherapy drove significant metabolic reprogramming in tumor cells and macrophages.
evidence: This claim is supported by the functional enrichment analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Two subtypes of macrophages were identified: Anti-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+CD86+) and Pro-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+ARG+).
source: We identified two subtypes of macrophages: Anti-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+CD86+) and Pro-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+ARG +) and sorted them by flow cytometry.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry analysis.

claim: The proportion of Pro-mac cells in LUAD tissues increased significantly after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
source: The proportion of Pro-mac cells in LUAD tissues increased significantly after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pro-mac cells promote tumor growth and angiogenesis and also suppress tumor immunity.
source: Pro-mac cells promote tumor growth and angiogenesis and also suppress tumor immunity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro and in vivo assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Chemotherapy ignited a relatively more robust immune cytotoxic response toward tumor cells.
source: Moreover, by analyzing the remodeling of T and B cells induced by neoadjuvant therapy, we noted that chemotherapy ignited a relatively more robust immune cytotoxic response toward tumor cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis of T and B cell data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nine patients with non-metastatic LUAD underwent lobectomy with curative intent in the Department of Thoracic Surgery, Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University.
source: A total of nine patients with non-metastatic LUAD underwent lobectomy with curative intent in the Department of Thoracic Surgery, Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University.
evidence: This claim is supported by the description of the study cohort in the manuscript.

claim: Five patients received three cycles of preoperative neoadjuvant combination chemotherapy with cisplatin plus pemetrexed.
source: Among them, five received three cycles of preoperative neoadjuvant combination chemotherapy with cisplatin plus pemetrexed (defined as NCT group), while others only received surgery (defined as the control group).
evidence: This claim is supported by the description of the treatment regimens in the manuscript.

claim: Cell clusters were classified using the Seurat package and relative marker genes through dimensional reduction and unsupervised clustering.
source: Next, we classified cell types through dimensional reduction and unsupervised clustering using the Seurat package and relative maker genes.
evidence: This claim describes the computational methods used in the study.

claim: Epithelial cells were marked by SFTA2 and KRT8.
source: Using the SingleR package, the CellMarker dataset, and our previous studies (Chen et al., 2021b; Chen et al., 2021a), we identified cell clusters that could be assigned to known cell lineages: epithelial cells (marked by SFTA2 and KRT8)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis and citations to previous studies.

claim: T cells were marked by CD3D and TRBC2.
source: T cells (marked by CD3D and TRBC2)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: B cells were marked by CD79A and CD19.
source: B cells (marked by CD79A and CD19)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Endothelial cells were marked by EMCN and CXorf36.
source: endothelial cells (ECs, marked by EMCN and CXorf36)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mast cells were marked by TPSB2 and TPSAB1.
source: mast cells (marked by TPSB2 and TPSAB1)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Macrophages were marked by CD68 and APOE.
source: macrophages (marked by CD68 and APOE)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Monocytes were marked by FGL2 and LGALS2.
source: monocytes (marked by FGL2 and LGALS2)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Fibroblasts were marked by LUM and DCN.
source: fibroblasts (marked by LUM and DCN)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Neutrophils were marked by FCGR3B and CMTM2.
source: neutrophils (marked by FCGR3B and CMTM2)
evidence: This claim is supported by the marker gene analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The proportion of cells other than tumor cells, especially immune cells (mainly T and B), was significantly higher in the NCT group.
source: By comparing the composition of different types of cells in each group, we noticed TME heterogeneity: the proportion of cells other than tumor cells, especially immune cells (mainly T and B), was significantly higher in the NCT (Figure 1e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and referenced in Figure 1e.

claim: The epithelial subclusters, mainly composed of cancer cells, were highly patient-specific.
source: Interestingly, the epithelial subclusters, mainly composed of cancer cells, were highly patient-specific, while the immune cell subclusters mostly consisted of cells derived from four or more patients (Figure 1f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and referenced in Figure 1f.

claim: The immune cell subclusters mostly consisted of cells derived from four or more patients.
source: Interestingly, the epithelial subclusters, mainly composed of cancer cells, were highly patient-specific, while the immune cell subclusters mostly consisted of cells derived from four or more patients (Figure 1f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and referenced in Figure 1f.

claim: More significantly upregulated metabolic pathways were enriched in cancer cells, nonmalignant epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and macrophages in the NCT group.
source: In each type of cell derived from the control and NCT groups, more significantly upregulated metabolic pathways were enriched in cancer cells, nonmalignant epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and macrophages (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and referenced in Figure 2a.

claim: The enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), glycolysis, pyruvate metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle indicates active glucose metabolism in cancer cells, nonmalignant epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and macrophages.
source: The enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), glycolysis, pyruvate metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle indicates active glucose metabolism in these four cell types.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the metabolic pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: The activity scores of the metabolic pathways of tumor cells and macrophages were significantly higher than those of other types of cells.
source: By analyzing the activity of metabolic pathways in cells from different sources, we found that the activity scores of the metabolic pathways of tumor cells and macrophages were significantly higher than those of other types of cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the metabolic pathway activity analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The metabolic pathway activity of macrophages and malignant cells increased after chemotherapy.
source: Notably, the metabolic pathway activity of macrophages and malignant cells increased after chemotherapy (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and referenced in Figure 2b.

claim: The proportion of malignant cells was significantly reduced after chemotherapy.
source: We found that the proportion of malignant cells was significantly reduced after chemotherapy (Figure 3b and c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and referenced in Figure 3b, 3c, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: MalignantNCT cells exhibited significantly higher malignant scores compared to MalignantSA cells.
source: Although malignant cells were significantly reduced after chemotherapy, genetic aberrations by CNVs analysis revealed that MalignantNCT cells exhibited significantly higher malignant scores compared to MalignantSA cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by CNV analysis data and referenced in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Nonmalignant cells evolved in two directions during pseudotime analysis.
source: Pseudotime analysis showed that nonmalignant cells evolved in two directions.
evidence: This claim is supported by pseudotime trajectory analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Glycolysis-related genes (ENO1, LDHB, GAPDH) gradually increased over time in the pseudotime analysis during epithelial cell transformation.
source: In this evolutionary process, glycolysis-related genes (ENO1, LDHB, GAPDH), OXPHOS-related genes (NDUFA4), mitochondrial repair-related genes (TOMM7), glucose and lipid metabolism regulation genes (S100A16), ATPase activity-related genes (CCT6A), tumor immune regulation-related genes (CCL20, CXCL1, PAEP, PPP1R14B), hypoxia response regulation genes (CHCHD2), apoptosis regulation genes (MEG3, CEACAM5), mRNA alternative splicing-related genes (LSM5), and Ras-related protein (RAC1, RALA) gradually increased over time in the pseudotime analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by pseudotime trajectory analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The activity of the glycolysis pathway, OXPHOS pathway, angiogenesis pathway, DNA repair pathway, and mTORC1 signaling pathway gradually increased during the transformation of epithelial cells into malignant tumor cells.
source: Correspondingly, during the process of epithelial cells transforming into malignant tumor cells, the activity of the glycolysis pathway, OXPHOS pathway, angiogenesis pathway, DNA repair pathway, and mTORC1 signaling pathway gradually increased over time.
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway activity analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: P53 pathway and apoptosis signaling pathway activity steadily decreased during the transformation of epithelial cells into malignant tumor cells.
source: However, P53 pathway, apoptosis signaling pathway activity then steadily decreased (Figure 3—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway activity analysis data and referenced in Figure 3—figure supplement 1f.

claim: The glycolysis pathway, OXPHOS pathway, MYC-targets, E2F-targets, DNA repair pathway, and mTORC1 signaling pathway were significantly enriched in MalignantNCT cells derived from the NCT group.
source: We found that the glycolysis pathway, OXPHOS pathway, MYC-targets, E2F-targets, DNA repair pathway, and mTORC1 signaling pathway were significantly enriched in MalignantNCT cells derived from the NCT group (Figure 3g).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 3g.

claim: Metabolic reprogramming enables cancer cells to resist anticancer drugs, thereby developing chemoresistance.
source: The metabolic reprogramming enables cancer cells to resist anticancer drugs, thereby developing chemoresistance (Tuerhong et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Tuerhong et al., 2021).

claim: E2F1, BRCA1, PURA, NKX2-1, NFIC, ETV7, STAT1, EGR1, and CEBPD were highly expressed in malignant cells from the control group.
source: To find the hub genes that cause the malignant transformation of epithelial cells, through Single-Cell Regulatory Network Inference and Clustering (SCENIC) analysis, we found that E2F1, BRCA1, PURA, NKX2-1, NFIC, ETV7, STAT1, EGR1, and CEBPD were highly expressed in malignant cells (cluster 2, 6, 11) from the control group.
evidence: This claim is supported by SCENIC analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Malignant cells from the NCT group have high expression of transcription factors such as PATZ1, SIX5, BATF, IRF1, FOXA1, and CEBPG.
source: In contrast, the malignant cells from the NCT group (clusters 1, 7, 8, 9) have a high expression of transcription factors (TFs) such as PATZ1, SIX5, BATF, IRF1, FOXA1, and CEBPG.
evidence: This claim is supported by SCENIC analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: After NCT, the increased expression of transcription factors promoted the occurrence of LUAD complex phenotypic remodeling.
source: After NCT, the increased expression of these TFs promoted the occurrence of LUAD complex phenotypic remodeling (Figure 3h).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the SCENIC analysis data and referenced in Figure 3h.

claim: Malignant cells were reclustered into 13 subclusters.
source: We reclustered the malignant cells and obtained 13 subclusters (Figure 3i and j).
evidence: This claim is supported by the clustering analysis data and referenced in Figure 3i and j.

claim: Clusters 5, 6, and 10 from the NCT group showed high levels of glycolysis, OXPHOS, and pyruvate metabolism.
source: Through the analysis of the metabolism of these cell subclusters, we found that clusters 5 (marker genes: PCP4/NPW/VSIG1), 6 (marker genes: ERG1/HSPA6), and 10 (marker genes: C9orf172/SLC39A10) from the NCT group showed high levels of glycolysis, OXPHOS, and pyruvate metabolism (Figure 3k).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolic analysis data and referenced in Figure 3k.

claim: NCT and immunotherapy significantly altered the stromal cell composition in the TME.
source: Therefore, this finding revealed that NCT and immunotherapy significantly altered the stromal cell composition in the TME.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the stromal cell composition analysis.

claim: Myofibroblasts exclusively originated from the control group.
source: In contrast, myofibroblasts exclusively originated from the control group.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cell composition analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Myofibroblasts have been described as cancer-associated fibroblasts that participate in extensive tissue remodeling, angiogenesis, and tumor progression.
source: According to previous research, myofibroblasts have been described as cancer-associated fibroblasts that participate in extensive tissue remodeling, angiogenesis, and tumor progression (Kim et al., 2020; Xie et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Kim et al., 2020; Xie et al., 2018).

claim: Endothelial 1 and 2 shared several upregulated pathways related to cell proliferation and fate regulation, including IL6-JAK-STAT3, TGFβ, and WNT-β catenin signaling.
source: In particular, GSVA exhibited that endothelial 1 and 2 shared several upregulated pathways related to cell proliferation and fate regulation, including IL6-JAK-STAT3, TGFβ, and WNT-β catenin signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pathways associated with energy metabolisms such as glycolysis and hypoxia were upregulated in myofibroblast.
source: Besides, pathways associated with energy metabolisms such as glycolysis and hypoxia were upregulated in myofibroblast, whereas pericyte was characterized by enriched OXPHOS and adipogenesis (Figure 4d).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 4d.

claim: Pericyte was characterized by enriched OXPHOS and adipogenesis.
source: Besides, pathways associated with energy metabolisms such as glycolysis and hypoxia were upregulated in myofibroblast, whereas pericyte was characterized by enriched OXPHOS and adipogenesis (Figure 4d).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 4d.

claim: Stromal cells exhibited enhanced metabolic levels after NCT, as represented by upregulated glycolysis, OXPHOS, and fatty acid metabolism pathways.
source: Meanwhile, when comparing the GSVA scores of these biological processes between patients from the control or NCT groups, we noted that the stromal cells exhibited enhanced metabolic levels after NCT, as represented by upregulated glycolysis, OXPHOS, and fatty acid metabolism pathways (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 4e.

claim: Fibroblasts were reclustered into 10 subgroups.
source: Considering the essential role of fibroblasts and their complicated function in shaping the TME, we further reclustered them into 10 subgroups (Figure 4f–h).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis data and referenced in Figure 4f-h.

claim: The GSVA score of metabolic pathways, including glycolysis and OXPHOS, and pyruvate metabolism and citrate cycle (TCA cycle), were upregulated in fibroblast clusters 5, 6, and 9.
source: As shown in Figure 4i and j, the GSVA score of the metabolic pathways, including glycolysis and OXPHOS, and pyruvate metabolism and citrate cycle (TCA cycle), were upregulated in clusters 5, 6, and 9.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 4i and j.

claim: The upregulation of metabolic pathways in fibroblast clusters 5, 6, and 9 was mainly observed in the NCT groups.
source: Intriguingly, the upregulation of these pathways was mainly observed in the NCT groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a and b.

claim: MEF2C, NFIA, and RAD21 might drive the formation of fibroblast clusters 5, 6, and 9, respectively.
source: Besides, the SCENIC analysis demonstrated that MEF2C, NFIA, and RAD21 might drive the formation of these clusters, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This claim is based on SCENIC analysis data and referenced in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Cellular dynamics in stromal cells support a consistent phenotypic shift of fibroblasts toward an increased metabolic level after preoperative chemotherapy.
source: Conclusively, cellular dynamics in stromal cells support a consistent phenotypic shift of fibroblasts toward an increased metabolic level after preoperative chemotherapy.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the stromal cell analysis data.

claim: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) have an essential influence on the inflammatory response in the TME.
source: In the process of cancer formation, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) have an essential influence on the inflammatory response in the TME (Malfitano et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Malfitano et al., 2020).

claim: All macrophages (10,526 cells) were reclustered into 10 cell clusters.
source: To study the effects of chemotherapy on TAMs, we first extracted all macrophages (10,526 cells) and reclustered them into 10 cell clusters (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis data and referenced in Figure 5a.

claim: The proportion of macrophages after chemotherapy was reduced.
source: From Figure 1e, we can see that the proportion of macrophages after chemotherapy was reduced.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell composition data and referenced in Figure 1e.

claim: Glycolysis, angiogenesis, PI3K-AKT-mTOR-signaling, IL6-JAK-STAT3-signaling, hypoxia, TGF-β-signaling were significantly enriched in macrophage clusters 0/1/8.
source: Through the GSVA, we found that glycolysis, angiogenesis, PI3K-AKT-mTOR-signaling, IL6-JAK-STAT3-signaling, hypoxia, TGF-β-signaling, and other signaling pathways were significantly enriched in clusters 0/1/8.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Promoting inflammation-related signaling pathways such as TNF signaling via NFKB, inflammatory response, Notch signaling, fatty acid metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation were increased dramatically in macrophage clusters 2/4/7/9.
source: Promoting inflammation-related signaling pathways such as TNF signaling via NFKB, inflammatory response, Notch signaling, fatty acid metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation were increased dramatically in clusters 2/4/7/9 (Figure 5d).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 5d.

claim: Glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism, alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism were more active in macrophage clusters 0/1/8.
source: Similarly, we found that glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism, alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism were more active in the clusters 0/1/8.
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolic pathway activity analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: OXPHOS, citrate cycle, pyruvate metabolism, fatty acid elongation, fatty acid biosynthesis were more active in macrophage clusters 2/4/7/9.
source: In contrast, OXPHOS, citrate cycle, pyruvate metabolism, fatty acid elongation, fatty acid biosynthesis, etc., were more active in clusters 2/4/7/9 (Figure 5e).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolic pathway activity analysis data and referenced in Figure 5e.

claim: The glycolysis/gluconeogenesis signaling pathway was significantly enriched in macrophages from the NCT group.
source: According to the GSVA, the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis signaling pathway was significantly enriched in macrophages from the NCT group.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Macrophages from the control group showed high activity in OXPHOS, fatty acid elongation, fatty acid degradation, fatty acid biosynthesis, and citrate cycle (TCA cycle).
source: In contrast, macrophages from the control group showed a high activity in OXPHOS, fatty acid elongation, fatty acid degradation, fatty acid biosynthesis, and citrate cycle (TCA cycle) (Figure 5f).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSVA analysis data and referenced in Figure 5f.

claim: Chemotherapy could promote glycolysis of TAMs and inhibit fatty acid metabolism.
source: In general, our results revealed that chemotherapy could promote glycolysis of TAMs and inhibit fatty acid metabolism.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the metabolic analysis data.

claim: HES, PPARG, SPI1, CEBPB, and IRF7 were highly expressed in macrophage cluster 0/1, which may be the key genes that regulate the conversion of macrophages into M2-like TAMs.
source: We found that HES, PPARG, SPI1, CEBPB, and IRF7 were highly expressed in cluster 0/1, which may be the key genes that regulate the conversion of macrophages into M2-like TAMs, while clusters 2/4/7/9 highly expressed STAT1, STAT2, NFKB1, JUN, and FOS that regulate the conversion of macrophages to M1-like TAMs (Figure 5g).
evidence: This claim is based on SCENIC analysis data and referenced in Figure 5g.

claim: Macrophage clusters 2/4/7/9 highly expressed STAT1, STAT2, NFKB1, JUN, and FOS that regulate the conversion of macrophages to M1-like TAMs.
source: We found that HES, PPARG, SPI1, CEBPB, and IRF7 were highly expressed in cluster 0/1, which may be the key genes that regulate the conversion of macrophages into M2-like TAMs, while clusters 2/4/7/9 highly expressed STAT1, STAT2, NFKB1, JUN, and FOS that regulate the conversion of macrophages to M1-like TAMs (Figure 5g).
evidence: This claim is based on SCENIC analysis data and referenced in Figure 5g.

claim: Macrophage clusters 0/1/8 exhibited M2-like polarization and anti-inflammatory properties.
source: Similarly, we found that 0/1/8 cluster cells exhibited M2-like polarization and anti-inflammatory properties, while 2/4/7/9 exhibited M1-like polarization and pro-inflammatory properties (Figure 5i).
evidence: This claim is supported by polarization and inflammatory scoring analysis and referenced in Figure 5i.

claim: Macrophage clusters 2/4/7/9 exhibited M1-like polarization and pro-inflammatory properties.
source: Similarly, we found that 0/1/8 cluster cells exhibited M2-like polarization and anti-inflammatory properties, while 2/4/7/9 exhibited M1-like polarization and pro-inflammatory properties (Figure 5i).
evidence: This claim is supported by polarization and inflammatory scoring analysis and referenced in Figure 5i.

claim: The 10 clusters of macrophage subtypes were divided into three categories: M1-like polarized phenotype (Anti-mac), M2-like polarized phenotype (Pro-mac), and those without obvious polarized phenotype (Mix).
source: Based on these analyses, we divided these 10 clusters of macrophage subtypes into three categories: M1-like polarized phenotype was defined as Anti-mac; M2-like polarized phenotype was defined as Pro-mac; and those without obvious polarized phenotype were defined as Mix (Figure 5j).
evidence: This claim is supported by the macrophage classification analysis and referenced in Figure 5j.

claim: The proportion of Pro-mac in the TME increased after chemotherapy.
source: We found that the proportion of Pro-mac in the TME increased after chemotherapy, especially in the case of NCT-1 (Figure 5k).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell composition analysis data and referenced in Figure 5k.

claim: Two subtypes, Anti-mac and Mix, can be converted to Pro-mac via trajectory analysis.
source: Interestingly, via trajectory analysis we found that two subtypes, Anti-mac and Mix, can be converted to Pro-mac.
evidence: This claim is supported by trajectory analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The high expression of LYZ, FBP1, ALOX5AP, MARCO, S100A9, FN1, CXCL8, APOC1CTSL may have played an essential role in promoting the conversion of Anti-mac to Pro-mac.
source: In this evolution process, the high expression of LYZ, FBP1, ALOX5AP, MARCO, S100A9, FN1, CXCL8, APOC1CTSL, and other genes may have played an essential role in promoting the conversion of Anti-mac to Pro-mac (Figure 5l and m).
evidence: This claim is based on trajectory analysis data and referenced in Figure 5l and m.

claim: Pro-mac was mainly characterized by high expression of CXCL8, ARG1, CREM, CD206, STAT6, CCL22, MMP7, and CCL3L3.
source: Pro-mac was mainly characterized by high expression of CXCL8, ARG1, CREM, CD206, STAT6, CCL22, MMP7, and CCL3L3, while Anti-mac was mainly characterized by high expression of CD86, HLA-DR, PLAC8, CXCL10, COX2, IL15R, and SCGB3A1 (Figure 6a).
evidence: This claim is supported by marker gene analysis data and referenced in Figure 6a.

claim: Anti-mac was mainly characterized by high expression of CD86, HLA-DR, PLAC8, CXCL10, COX2, IL15R, and SCGB3A1.
source: Pro-mac was mainly characterized by high expression of CXCL8, ARG1, CREM, CD206, STAT6, CCL22, MMP7, and CCL3L3, while Anti-mac was mainly characterized by high expression of CD86, HLA-DR, PLAC8, CXCL10, COX2, IL15R, and SCGB3A1 (Figure 6a).
evidence: This claim is supported by marker gene analysis data and referenced in Figure 6a.

claim: Anti-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+CD86+) and Pro-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+ARG+) were sorted by flow cytometry.
source: Based on these marker genes, we sorted out Anti-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+CD86+) and Pro-mac cells (CD45+CD11b+ARG +) by flow cytometry (Figure 6b).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data and referenced in Figure 6b.

claim: The proportion of Pro-mac cells in LUAD tissues after NCT increased significantly.
source: Our results showed that the proportion of Pro-mac cells in LUAD tissues after NCT increased significantly (Figure 6d).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data and referenced in Figure 6d.

claim: The proportion of cells marked by the marker gene CD206 of M2-like TAMs increased significantly after chemotherapy.
source: In fact, by performing immunofluorescence staining on LUAD tissue samples derived from surgery alone and NCT, we also found that the proportion of cells marked by the marker gene CD206 of M2-like TAMs increased significantly after chemotherapy (Figure 6e).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data and referenced in Figure 6e.

claim: IL10, PDCD1LG2, PDGF, VEGF, MMP9, CXCL9, CXCR4, IL22, KLF4, and TGF-β were highly expressed in Pro-mac cells that promote tumor growth, angiogenesis, and suppress tumor immunity.
source: By analyzing the differentially expressed genes of Pro-mac and Anti-mac cells, we found IL10, PDCD1LG2, PDGF, VEGF, MMP9, CXCL9, CXCR4, IL22, KLF4, and TGF-β were highly expressed in Pro-mac cells that promote tumor growth, angiogenesis, and suppress tumor immunity (Figure 6f).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential gene expression analysis and referenced in Figure 6f.

claim: The levels of MMP9, EGF, and VEGF secreted by Pro-mac after NCT were significantly higher than those of Pro-mac from the surgery alone group.
source: The levels of MMP9, EGF, and VEGF secreted by Pro-mac after NCT were significantly higher than those of Pro-mac from the surgery alone group.
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data presented in the manuscript.

claim: MMP9, EGF, VEGF, and IL10 secreted by Pro-mac were significantly higher than Anti-mac.
source: MMP9, EGF, VEGF, and IL10 secreted by Pro-mac were significantly higher than Anti-mac (Figure 6g).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data and referenced in Figure 6g.

claim: NCT Pro-mac can significantly promote tumor growth in vivo.

claim: Glycolysis could enhance the ability of Pro-mac to promote tumor progression and increase the capacity of Anti-mac to inhibit tumors.

claim: 22,530 T cells were detected, which accounted for 26.9% of the total cells.

claim: T cells were divided into CD4+ T (marked by LTB, CD45RO, etc.), CD8+ T (marked by NKG7, GZMA, GZMB, CD8A, etc.), and Tregs (marked by FOXP3, CTLA4, etc.).
source: According to the expression of a series of canonical markers of T cell subtypes, the T cells were divided into CD4+ T (marked by LTB, CD45RO, etc.), CD8+ T (marked by NKG7, GZMA, GZMB, CD8A, etc.), and Tregs (marked by FOXP3, CTLA4, etc.) (Lambrechts et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2021b; Lu et al., 2020; Figure 6—figure supplement 1c and d).

claim: NCT treatment ignites a relatively more robust immune cytotoxic response toward tumor cells.

claim: The mixed glycolysis/OXPHOS phenotype significantly promotes aggressiveness and treatment resistance.
source: Therefore, recent research emphasizes the mixed glycolysis/OXPHOS phenotype rather than the phenotype that relies excessively on glycolysis to meet cellular energy requirements, thereby significantly promoting aggressiveness and treatment resistance (Jia et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Jia et al., 2018).

claim: Chemical drugs can activate the tissue damage repair mechanism dominated by TAM, which will cause tumors to grow rapidly and patients to develop resistance to antitumor chemotherapy.
source: Theoretically, chemical drugs can inhibit tumorigenesis by blocking the proliferation of tumor cells or depositing in tumor cell apoptosis, but this unintentionally causes 'tissue damage'. The body will mistake this tumor-specific damage for normal tissue damage and then inevitably activate the tissue damage repair mechanism dominated by TAM (Pathria et al., 2019). The result of this effect is that tumors will grow rapidly, and patients will develop resistance to antitumor chemotherapy.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Pathria et al., 2019) and inference.

claim: NCT exerted PD-L1 upregulation in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients and increased the density of CD68+ macrophages, which were associated with better outcomes.
source: Meanwhile, as suggested by Parra et al., NCT exerted PD-L1 upregulation in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. It increased the density of CD68+ macrophages, which were associated with better outcomes in both univariate and multivariate analyses (Parra et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Parra et al., 2018).

claim: NSCLC patients treated with radiotherapy displayed a decrease in lymphoid cells and a relative increase in macrophages.

evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published research (Talebian Yazdi et al., 2016).
